literal: The pallor of the eyes has indeed attained distress, having seen what the bright-foreheaded lady did.
translation: Seeing the self-afflicting grief of this bright-foreheaded lady, even the pallor of her eyes seems to have fallen into deep distress.
modern: ஒளிபொருந்திய நெற்றியை உடையவள் தனக்குத்தானே செய்து கொண்ட துன்பத்தைக் கண்டு, அவளுடைய கண்களில் படர்ந்த பசலை நிறமும் கூடத் துன்பத்தை அடைந்துவிட்டது.
explanation: This couplet describes the extreme state of the heroine's grief during separation from her lover. Her eyes have developed 'pasappu', a pale, sallow discoloration that signifies deep yearning. The poet beautifully personifies this pallor, suggesting that even the pallor itself has become distressed upon witnessing how much the bright-foreheaded lady ('ஒண்ணுதல்') is suffering. Instead of merely being a symptom of her pain, the pallor is depicted as a sympathetic observer that is overwhelmed by her sorrow.
